newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK SAYS TO SIGN $50MLN CREDIT FACILITY.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK SAYS TO SIGN $50MLN CREDIT FACILITY.

text.p: Slovakia's largest steel producer, VSZ a.s., said on Friday it would sign a five-year, $50 million revolving syndicated credit facility, lead-managed by Chase Manhattan, later in the day.
"We should sign a syndicated loan with Chase Manhattan and other banks today to finance the investment plans of VSZ a.s.," Jozef Burian, head of VSZ's financial department told Reuters.
He declined to provide further details at this stage.
Burian said the loan would be mainly used for investment within the company.
VSZ unveiled plans last year for investment in central Europe but has not given any details of progress.
Slovakia's Investicna a Rozvojova Banka, in which VSZ has a controlling stake, said on Thursday that its president and three other board members had been replaced at VSZ's request.
Earlier this month, Burian told Reuters the company was also considering an international bond issue at the end of this year or in the beginning of 1998.
